transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Since I stopped working full-time, I keep starting projects for the museum and then just never finishing them, even when I really want to. It’s been really frustrating because I want to do a good job, but I just can't seem to see things through to the end.

Before you stopped working full-time, did you have similar problems with staying organized, finishing tasks, or getting distracted, even back in childhood or school? Or did this mainly start after your work situation changed?

To be honest, these issues go all the way back to childhood—my elementary school teachers always said I was bright but constantly daydreaming and forgetting to hand in my homework. Working as a handyman kept me on track because it was so hands-on, but once I retired and started this museum planning work, these lifelong tendencies really came to a head.

Do these attention and organization problems affect you in more than one part of your life now, such as at home, with paperwork, hobbies, or relationships, and not just with the museum projects? Can you give one or two examples?

Yes, it definitely affects other parts of my life, especially at home and with my hobbies. For instance, my wife will tell me a meeting time while I'm looking right at her, but the words don't register and I have to ask her to repeat it minutes later. Also, with my photography, I get easily sidetracked sorting through old archives instead of finishing the actual projects I planned.

Along with the attention and organization problems, have you also had lifelong issues with restlessness, feeling driven to keep moving, interrupting others, or acting before thinking? Or has it mainly been the inattentive side?

It has definitely been mainly the inattentive side, as I've never really struggled with physical restlessness, impulsivity, or interrupting people. Even when I was a kid, my teachers always complained about my daydreaming and losing track of things, never about me being hyperactive or disruptive.

Have these attention problems caused clear problems in your life over time, like poor grades, repeated mistakes at work, missed bills or appointments, or strain in relationships? What are the main examples?

Yes, they've caused issues throughout my life; in grade school, I'd constantly daydream, lose track of instructions, and forget to hand in homework I'd actually completed. Since retiring, my spacing out has led to me double-booking rooms and missing email deadlines at the museum, which makes me feel unreliable and hesitant to take on new responsibilities.
